fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Florida as a Constructed Mythic Place", "body": "Juan anchored the evening in a 1993 essay called Florida's Fudged Identity, reading lines that called the state a hologram of paradise and a state of mind as much as a state of being. He argued the essay hinted that Florida's history had largely been made up, and he noted that Henry Flagler, Henry Plant and Henry Sanford pushed into what he called the last frontier. Later he returned to the same essay for a passage on Epcot, claiming Disney and nearby communities had imitated each other into a mirrored reality inside a reality."}, {"title": "Mirror Magic and the Three Souls", "body": "Juan traced a mirror motif through Florida's deep past. He said the indigenous people of the Keys, whom he named as the Tequesta, believed humans carried three souls, one in the eyes, one in the shadow and one in the reflection, and he cautioned that Spanish accounts of their worship, such as a stuffed deer, were probably propaganda. He tied the idea to Aztec mirror lore around John Dee and to a talk he and Thomas had given on Benjamin Paul Blood, who described staring into a mirror and wondering whether he faced another reality."}, {"title": "John Dee and the Enochian Calls", "body": "One speaker noted that the show landed on John Dee's birthday and called Dee a heightened character of the region, and Thomas announced he was working on a comic book about Dee and Edward Kelly. One guest described Dee and Kelly carrying angelic messages to Emperor Rudolph II, while another speaker added that the Voynich manuscript changed hands at that meeting. A guest also wondered whether the 48 main Enochian calls might map onto the lower 48 states, while warning that the calls were said to bring forth the end of the world."}, {"title": "Hidden Geometry in Maps and Buildings", "body": "Gabe shared a graphic placing Rhode Island at 41 north and 71 west and Jekyll Island at 31 north and 81 west, calling it an exact linear progression, and said that triangulating from those points led him to the Chicxulub impact crater. Homie Romie argued that shape mattered for transmutation, saying you needed the right oven to bake a cake. He described the earth as a Merkaba and the rotundas of US Capitol buildings as places where ascension passed through the oculus."}, {"title": "Astrotheology and the Coded Past", "body": "Chance argued that the likeliest conclusion was astrotheology, saying researchers had made that case for hundreds of years and that most ancient history encoded mythology and was probably mostly not real. Asked what he meant, he described the constellations as a codex for interpreting myths and languages across regions, and he suggested the sky was used because it reflected nature and was visible from anywhere in the world. Another speaker asked whether Atlantis might never have existed and might instead describe the high tech age we live in now."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: A few fellas native to Florida join the Rant tonight to de-occult the mysteries of America's wanged man, the Sunshine State. We've got Juan Ayala, Thomas Gorence, the Homie Romie, and Slick Dissident, on a full moon that's also John Dee's birthday. It's gonna get weird.
